name: The Royal Heritage Courtyard
subtitle: An illustrative exploration of classic Indian temple & palace architecture
description: An interactive digital reconstruction showcasing stone-carved colonnades, ornate jharokha balconies, sacred central pavilions, and geometric water reservoirs typical of medieval Rajasthani architecture.

galleryImages.caption: The Central Mandapa — Sacred octagonal pillared hall featuring corbelled dome and carved lintels.
Projected Stone Jharokha — Overhanging sandstone balcony engineered for privacy and convective cooling.
Geometric Baori Stepwell — Symmetrical descending stone terraces engineered for rainwater retention.
Ceremonial Torana Gateway — Monumental carved threshold framing the entrance into the sacred courtyard.

highlights.title: Central Mandapa (Pillared Hall)
highlights.description: An octagonal assembly hall with eight load-bearing pillars supporting a corbelled floral dome.

highlights.title: Ornate Stone Jharokha
highlights.description: A cantilevered enclosed balcony with delicate pierced jali screens providing natural shade.

highlights.title: Geometric Stepwell (Baori)
highlights.description: A subterranean geometric pool capturing desert rainfall while cooling the surrounding courtyard.

highlights.title: Monolithic Torana Gateway
highlights.description: A ceremonial arched portal adorned with mythical makara carvings marking the precinct threshold.

highlights.title: Venturi Jali Screens
highlights.description: Perforated stone panels that compress air passing through, lowering internal temperatures naturally.

historicalContext.significance: Illustrates how ancient and medieval Indian builders harmonized sacred geometry, passive cooling, and hydraulic engineering in arid desert climates.
detailedStory: The Royal Heritage Courtyard is conceived as an educational digital model synthesising the finest architectural principles of Western Indian palaces, havelis, and temple mandapas. Rather than claiming to be a photographic replica of a single protected monument, this environment accurately represents the structural elements common to Shekhawati havelis, Marwar desert forts, and Gurjara-Pratihara pillared halls.

Traditional courtyards functioned as the spiritual and climatic lungs of a building complex. Deep colonnaded verandas shaded the living quarters from searing midday heat, while the central open skylight created a chimney effect, drawing cool evening breezes across sunken water basins.

Every ornamental detail in this reconstruction—from the lotus medallions carved into the pillar brackets to the fine floral latticework of the jharokha screens—has been cross-referenced with surviving 16th and 17th-century heritage structures across Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, and Shekhawati.

name: Konark Sun Sanctuary
subtitle: The monumental stone chariot of the Sun God Surya
description: An upcoming interactive 3D digital recreation of the 13th-century Kalinga masterpiece, featuring colossal carved stone wheels that function as precise solar sundials.

highlights.title: Astronomical Chariot Wheels
highlights.description: Twelve pairs of intricately sculpted stone wheels capable of telling exact time by shadow angles.

highlights.title: Nata Mandir (Dance Pavilion)
highlights.description: Pillared ceremonial hall carved with thousands of figures in classical Odissi dance postures.

historicalContext.significance: UNESCO World Heritage monument celebrated as one of India's paramount architectural and astronomical achievements.
detailedStory: Conceived as a colossal chariot drawn by seven galloping horses across the heavens, the Sun Temple at Konark represents the zenith of medieval stone sculpture.
Upcoming digital recreation under research for future release in NewArambh.

name: Diwan-i-Khas Mirror Pavilion
subtitle: The shimmering Sheesh Mahal of Amber Fort
description: An upcoming 3D exploration of Raja Man Singh's palace, where thousands of convex Belgian mirrors embedded into floral plaster create a cosmos of starlight under candlelight.

highlights.title: Sheesh Mahal Mirror Murals
highlights.description: Thousands of miniature glass pieces reflecting flickering candlelight across the vaulted ceiling.

historicalContext.significance: A hilltop fortress palace combining impenetrable outer ramparts with delicate, jeweled inner royal courts.
detailedStory: Upcoming digital recreation under research for future release in NewArambh.

name: Nalanda Ancient Monastic University
subtitle: The legendary seat of universal Buddhist learning
description: An upcoming digital architectural model of ancient Nalanda's red brick monasteries, meditation stupas, and grand tiered lecture courtyards from the Gupta era.

highlights.title: Great Stupa No. 3
highlights.description: Tiered votive stupa with carved stucco sculptures of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas.

historicalContext.significance: One of the world's first residential universities, hosting over 10,000 scholars from across Asia.
detailedStory: Upcoming digital recreation under research for future release in NewArambh.

name: Thousand Pillar Colonnade
subtitle: The sculpted stone labyrinth of Meenakshi Amman
description: An upcoming 3D exploration of Madurai's iconic Aayiram Kaal Mandapam, where 985 carved granite pillars form a breathtaking forest of mythological figures.

highlights.title: Yali Guardian Columns
highlights.description: Monolithic pillars carved with roaring Yali creatures holding stone balls inside their jaws.

historicalContext.significance: Masterpiece of south Indian stone engineering with acoustic musical pillars.
detailedStory: Upcoming digital recreation under research for future release in NewArambh.

name: Kailasa Monolithic Cliff Sanctuary
subtitle: The rock-cut mountain carved top-down from living stone
description: An upcoming 3D exploration of Cave 16 at Ellora—the largest monolithic rock-cut monument on Earth, excavated entirely by hand using chisels and hammers.
period: 8th Century CE (Rashtrakuta Dynasty, King Krishna I)

highlights.title: Ravana Shaking Mount Kailasa
highlights.description: Dramatic multi-tiered narrative relief carved directly into the bedrock cliff face.

historicalContext.significance: Over 200,000 tonnes of basalt rock were removed from top to bottom over two centuries.
detailedStory: Upcoming digital recreation under research for future release in NewArambh.
